reason: The text describes preparations for the theophany at Mount Sinai (Exodus 19). Throughout this passage, the Hebrew people do not speak at all, nor do they voice any criticism or complaint. The only speakers are God and Moses. Moses relays God's commands regarding sanctification and boundary-setting, and makes one statement to God acknowledging the people cannot ascend the mountain (due to the sacred boundaries God has established), but this is not a voicing of criticism—it is Moses' acknowledgment of divine instruction. The people remain silent and obedient, with no articulated grievance against either their leaders or Yahweh.
